data.name: Lisan
data.gender_notes: Lisan is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root ‘l-s-n’, which means ‘tongue’ or ‘speech’. In Islamic context, Lisan can symbolize the power of articulate speech and the importance of expressing truth and wisdom. The Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) is reported to have said, ‘A man speaking the truth will be saved from the Hell-fire, even if he has committed actions equal to the fill of the earth.’ (Sahih Muslim).
data.spiritual_meaning: Articulate speech that expresses truth and wisdom
data.etymology: Lisan belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Tongue, Speech.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Lisan total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_arabic.name: لسان
in_arabic.meaning: اللسان يعني اللسان أو الكلام أو التعبير عن الأفكار
in_arabic.long_meaning: اللسان هو اسم عربي مشتق من الفعل 'لسن' الذي يعني التكلم أو التعبير عن الأفكار والمشاعر. في اللغة العربية، اللسان هو العضو الذي يستخدم للتحدث والتواصل. وفي القرآن الكريم، يوصف اللسان بأنه أداة للتعبير عن الشكر والحمد لله. اسم لسان يحمل معاني متعددة، منها القدرة على التعبير والتواصل بفعالية، والصدق في القول، والوضوح في التعبير عن الأفكار والمشاعر.

in_urdu.name: لسان
in_urdu.meaning: لسان کا مطلب ہے زبان یا بولنے کی صلاحیت
in_urdu.long_meaning: نام لسان عربی زبان سے ماخوذ ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے زبان یا بولنے کی صلاحیت۔ یہ نام اس بات کی علامت ہے کہ انسان اپنی زبان سے اپنے افکار اور مشاعر کو ظاہر کر سکتا ہے۔ اسلامی روایات میں، لسان کو ایک ایسا ذریعہ سمجھا جاتا ہے جو انسان کو دوسروں کے ساتھ بات چیت کرنے اور اپنے خیالات کو واضح طریقے سے پیش کرنے کی صلاحیت प्रदान کرتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: लिसान
in_hindi.meaning: लिसान का अर्थ है जीभ या बोलने की क्षमता
in_hindi.long_meaning: लिसान नाम की उत्पत्ति अरबी भाषा से हुई है, जिसका अर्थ है जीभ या बोलने की क्षमता। यह नाम इस बात का प्रतीक है कि मनुष्य अपनी जीभ से अपने विचारों और भावनाओं को व्यक्त कर सकता है। इस्लामी परंपराओं में, लिसान को एक ऐसा माध्यम माना जाता है जो मनुष्य को दूसरों के साथ बातचीत करने और अपने विचारों को स्पष्ट तरीके से प्रस्तुत करने की क्षमता प्रदान करता है।

in_pashto.name: لسان
in_pashto.meaning: لسان دى معنى ژبه يا د خبرو کولو توانايي
in_pashto.long_meaning: د لسان نوم د عربي ژبې څخه اخيستل شوی دی، چې دى معنى ژبه يا د خبرو کولو توانايي. دا نوم د دې علامه ده چې انسان کولاى شي خپلى ژبې سره خپل فکرونه او احساسات څرګند کړي. په اسلامي دودونو کې، لسان داسې يو ذريعہ ګڼل کېږي چې انسان ته د نورو سره د خبرو اترو او خپلو افکارو د واضح ډول وړاندې کولو توانايي برابروي.

in_english.name: Lisan
in_english.meaning: Lisan means tongue or the ability to speak
in_english.long_meaning: The name Lisan is derived from Arabic, meaning 'tongue' or 'the ability to speak'. It symbolizes the capacity to express thoughts and emotions through language. In Islamic tradition, Lisan is considered a vital tool for communication, enabling individuals to convey their ideas and feelings effectively. The name also reflects the importance of articulate expression and honest communication in Islam.

pronunciation.pashto: په پښتو کې د تلفظ تفصیل: لسان

data.cultural_impact: In Arabic culture, Lisan is often associated with linguistic prowess, including eloquence, oratory skills, and the art of storytelling. Arabic poetry, for instance, often revolves around the theme of Lisan, emphasizing the power of words in expressing emotion, ideas, and experiences. In some traditions, a person who masters the Arabic language is also known as a ‘Shaheed-e-Lisan’, or ‘The Martyr of the Tongue’. This indicates a linguistic expertise and influencer, the ability to effect change through speech, making a notable cultural impact.
data.spiritual_significance: According to Islamic teachings, the tongue is considered one of the most powerful faculties of human beings. Controlled speech is considered a sign of the mercy of God, as it enables humans to express their emotions, thoughts, and wisdom in a beneficial way. On the other hand, unrestrained speech can lead to misinformation, harm, and misconceptions. Therefore, in Islamic spirituality, Lisan represents the importance of the power of words in communication, both within and without. It advocates using speech as a means to seek closeness to God, spread knowledge, and diffuse peace amongst people. Ultimately, Lisan serves as a reminder of the great potential of the tongue and encourages Muslims to strive for its ethical and productive use.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Abdul Barr in his book 'Al-Isti'ab' mentions Lisan Al-Din as a Persian physician who lived during the Abbasid Caliphate (750-1258 AD) and was renowned for his medical knowledge and expertise in pharmacology.

Al-Maqrizi in his book 'Kitab Al-Mawāqi' states that Lisan Al-Din Al-Fusi was a prominent Moroccan historian and geographer who lived during the late 14th and early 15th centuries (1353-1415 AD) and is considered one of the pioneers of Arabic historical writing.
